speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and have difficulty positioning your leg following a rear-end collision. To begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly how the injury occurred and what specific movements make the pain worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned immediate pain in both knees and severe right groin pain; were you wearing a seatbelt during the collision, and did you experience any loss of consciousness? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray, Right_Hip_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_X-ray: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text: The physical exam findings of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated right leg are classic for a hip dislocation, not appendicitis. text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

text: Thank you for that history. text:
